solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Can glib radio broadcast grab primarily enthusiastic TV man?

indicators.note: 'Primarily' points to the first letter of the word it follows.

blocks.note: A john is slang for a toilet, as is a can.
The letters to be rearranged.
First letter of enthusiastic.

explanation.surface: A smooth-talking radio presenter hopes to win over a keen television personality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' looks like a verb opening a question, but it is the noun: both can and john are slang for a lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: John Logie Baird was the Scottish inventor who gave the first public demonstration of television, so he is the original TV man.

clue.text: Fringes on women’s clothing no longer in fashion

blocks.note: What is no longer in fashion is out.
Skirts are women's clothing.

explanation.surface: Fringed trims on women's garments have gone out of style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringes on women's clothing' reads as one phrase about trimmings; the definition is just 'Fringes'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the outlying edges of a town are its fringes, the parts furthest from the centre.

clue.text: Ruth’s mother-in-law has complaint about setter

blocks.note: A moan is a complaint.
The setter refers to themself as I.

explanation.surface: A biblical in-law grumbles about the crossword compiler.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the person who wrote the puzzle, so 'setter' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth, Ruth is married to Naomi's son and stays loyal to Naomi after he dies.

clue.text: Drink soda? Not initially, with a green rum

indicators.note: Rum means odd, so the letters come out in an odd order.

blocks.note: Soda without its first letter S.
Taken as printed.
Taken as printed.

explanation.surface: Someone orders a mixer, then decides on a dubious green rum instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the spirit that goes with the soda, but it is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangeade is a fizzy orange-flavoured drink.

clue.text: Very small bits of moon visible before day is over

indicators.note: In a down answer, something turned over reads from the bottom up.

blocks.note: Io is one of Jupiter's moons.
SAT is the calendar abbreviation for Saturday.

explanation.surface: Tiny slivers of the moon show in the sky before daytime is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is over' reads as 'has ended', but it turns the day upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: An iota is a very small amount, from the smallest Greek letter.

clue.text: Representations of data portal used in London hospital

blocks.note: An arch is a portal or gateway.
Barts is St Bartholomew's, a famous London hospital.

explanation.surface: An online data portal is adopted by a London hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Data portal' reads as a website, but the portal is an arch; 'of data' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bar charts show data as bars of different lengths.

clue.text: Perhaps Eric Morecambe’s third appearance as layabout

blocks.note: Eric Idle of Monty Python is one Eric, so 'perhaps Eric' gives his surname.
The third letter of Morecambe.

explanation.surface: A famous comedian's third TV appearance casts him as a lazy character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eric Morecambe' reads as one comedian, but it splits: Eric points to another comic, Eric Idle, and Morecambe only lends its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An idler is someone who lazes about, a layabout.

clue.text: Drinking on the way home? Yes, if May

blocks.note: Downing a drink is drinking it.
A street is a way.

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they may have a drink on the way home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If May' looks like asking permission, but May is Theresa May, the former Prime Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Number 10 Downing Street is the Prime Minister's official home, so it was home to Theresa May.

clue.text: One of the Young Ones heading up Coward season

blocks.note: Spring is a season.
A chicken is a coward.

explanation.surface: A star of the sitcom The Young Ones leads a season of Noël Coward plays.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals mislead: The Young Ones was a British TV comedy and Noël Coward a playwright, but here they are just young people and a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: calling someone 'no spring chicken' means they are no longer young, so a spring chicken is a youngster.

clue.text: Courtyard piano – 8PM, here

blocks.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly.
The PM of 8 Down, Downing Street, is at No 10, so 'here' is AT 10, with 1 and 0 read as the letters I and O.

explanation.surface: A piano sits in the courtyard for an eight o'clock performance.
explanation.walkthrough: '8PM' looks like a time of day, but it is the Prime Minister of 8 Down, whose address is Number 10.
explanation.definitionFit: A patio is a paved courtyard beside a house.

clue.text: Where you might find worms in skylight after sunset?

blocks.note: A riddle: think of the word that worms follows to name a glowing insect.
The light lingering in the sky once the sun has gone down.

explanation.walkthrough: Read as AFTER GLOW, it is where the word worms goes to make glow-worms.
explanation.definitionFit: The afterglow is the light left in the sky after the sun has set.

clue.text: Hint: using Star Trek language’s not on

blocks.note: Writing in ink is writing using ink.
Klingon is the Star Trek alien language; without ON it is KLING.

explanation.surface: A tip that speaking Star Trek's alien language just isn't done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not on' reads as 'not acceptable', but it removes the ON from Klingon.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a faint notion of something, the kind of hint you half-grasp.

clue.text: Fantastic riches, penning first of zither movements

blocks.note: The letters to be rearranged.
First letter of zither.

explanation.surface: A composer earns vast wealth writing music for the zither.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movements' is the musical sense: scherzi is the Italian plural of scherzo.
explanation.definitionFit: Scherzi, plural of scherzo, are lively movements in a symphony or sonata.

clue.text: Liverpool player after own goal, about . . . . to do this?

definitions.text: Liverpool player after own goal, about . . . . to do this?

blocks.note: OG is the standard abbreviation for own goal.
Liverpool FC play in red and are known as the Reds.

explanation.surface: A Liverpool footballer who has just scored an own goal is about to do something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a player who has scored an own goal is likely to blush, to go red.
explanation.definitionFit: Going red is blushing, what an embarrassed footballer does after putting the ball in his own net.

clue.text: Pair playing dice more, having forgotten about writing a book

blocks.note: A duo is a pair.
The letters to be rearranged, before the removal.
RE, as in a memo's 're:', means about; these are the letters forgotten.
Surface padding: it gives the dice players a book to neglect.

explanation.surface: Two people keep playing dice and forget all about the book they should be writing.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the usual crossword word for 'about', as in a memo's 're:'.
explanation.definitionFit: A duodecimo is a small book, made from sheets folded into twelve leaves.

clue.text: When Prince upset singer, making false accusations

blocks.note: As can mean when, as in 'as I left'.
P is an abbreviation for Prince.
The letters to be rearranged.

explanation.surface: The pop star Prince offended another singer by spreading lies about them.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince reads as the musician, but it only gives its abbreviation P.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb asperse, from Latin for sprinkle, means to spatter someone with slander, so its participle means making false accusations.

clue.text: Someone that has other ranks to support sheriff’s men on ship

indicators.note: In a down answer, a support sits underneath.

blocks.note: A posse is a band of men gathered by a sheriff.
SS is the abbreviation for steamship.
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers.

explanation.surface: Enlisted soldiers back up a sheriff's posse aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces stack top to bottom: POSSE on SS, with OR underneath supporting them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an owner or holder, read as a noun phrase, 'someone that has'.

clue.text: Feature among distribution of aid on Asian peninsula

indicators.note: Distributing the letters spreads them into a new order.

blocks.note: The chin is a facial feature.
The letters to be rearranged.

explanation.surface: A report features the handing out of aid across a region of Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feature' reads as a news story, but it is a facial feature, the chin.
explanation.definitionFit: Indochina is the peninsula of South-East Asia holding Vietnam, Laos, Cambodia and neighbours.

clue.text: Service receivers never to be found in the wrong court, with mess unfolding

definitions.text: Service receivers never to be found in the wrong

blocks.note: The letters to be rearranged.
More letters to be rearranged.

explanation.surface: Someone is never found at fault in court, even as a mess unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The wrong court' looks like a legal slip, but 'never to be found in the wrong' belongs to the definition: the customer is always right.
explanation.definitionFit: Customers receive a service, and the saying goes that the customer is never wrong.

clue.text: See 9
Drinks with lawyer, in cry for help

blocks.note: SOS is the distress call.
A DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer.

explanation.surface: Someone out drinking with a lawyer ends up calling for help.
explanation.walkthrough: DA, district attorney, is the American title for a public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: soda water and other fizzy soft drinks are all drinks, and Americans call any of them a soda.

clue.text: See 8
What journo might say in print?

blocks.note: A riddle: how a reporter might introduce themself, naming their trade.
The verb sense: to stamp or press a mark on a surface.

explanation.walkthrough: Split as I'M PRESS, it is how a journalist introduces themself.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to print or stamp a mark on something.

clue.text: Tooth with nasty smell round top of root

indicators.note: In a down answer the top of a word is its first letter.

blocks.note: Pong is British slang for a bad smell.
First letter of root.

explanation.surface: A decaying tooth smells bad all around its root.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tooth' and 'root' suggest dentistry, but the tooth is a fork's.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the tool sense: each spike of a fork or rake is called a tooth.

clue.text: Puppet that’s small? Small and quiet

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels.
Wee is Scottish for small.
P is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly.

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a puppet is small, and is told it is small and quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweep is a squeaking grey dog puppet from the British children's show Sooty.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweep is a well-known glove puppet.

clue.text: Seductress flirting in Crete

blocks.note: The letters to be rearranged.

explanation.surface: A temptress flirts on a Greek island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flirting' looks like the seductress's action, but it is the signal to rearrange IN CRETE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a seductress lures and tempts, which is what one who entices does.

clue.text: Pitch first of tents below middle of scout pack

blocks.note: Pitch is a tar-like black substance.
Middle letter of scout.
First letter of tents.

explanation.surface: A scout pack is told to pitch its tents first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scout pack' reads as one phrase, but pack is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is a pack of cards used for fortune-telling.

clue.text: Rum showing in biscuit, said Prohibition agent

blocks.note: Cookie spoken sounds like kooky, which becomes KOOKI before -NESS.
Eliot Ness was the Prohibition agent who led the Untouchables.

explanation.surface: Rum turns up inside a biscuit, says a Prohibition agent looking for alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the liquor a Prohibition agent would hunt, but it means strange; the definition is read as the noun, rumness.
explanation.definitionFit: British 'rum' means odd, and 'kooky' means eccentric, so the quality of being either is the same.

clue.text: Rear light units, say

indicators.note: 'Say' asks for the word as spoken.

blocks.note: Rays are units of light, and 'say' asks for their sound.

explanation.surface: The lights at the back of a vehicle, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rear light' reads as a tail light, but Rear is the verb, as in rearing children.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the child-rearing sense: to bring up a family is both to rear and to raise it.

clue.text: Son with gripe about ceremonial song

blocks.note: Taken as printed, to be rearranged.
Taken as printed, to be rearranged.
Ritual means ceremonial.

explanation.surface: A son complains about a formal hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son' usually gives S, but here all three letters go into the mix with GRIPE; 'ceremonial song' reads as one phrase, but song alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Negro spiritual is a religious folk song of African American origin.
